title: Tenant-aware audit-forwarder with tiered retention and customer-managed storage integrations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware audit-forwarder that supports tiered retention semantics and first-class integrations with customer-managed storage backends for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments. The feature will provide: (1) per-tenant retention and cold-tiering policy enforcement; (2) secure uploads to customer-managed sinks (S3-compatible, Azure/GCS, SFTP, on-prem object appliances) using rotating signed URLs or brokered multipart uploads; (3) strong encryption and CMEK handshake patterns for customer keys; (4) resumable transfers and backpressure-aware buffering for constrained on-prem networks; (5) operational observability and end-to-end proof-of-delivery for compliance audits.
acceptance_criteria: Each tenant can configure a retention tier policy (hot, warm, cold) via the Console API and it is respected by the forwarder
Forwarder supports at least S3-compatible (pre-signed multipart), Azure Blob with SAS tokens, GCS signed URLs, and a configurable SFTP adapter for air-gapped appliances
CMEK handshake succeeds for customer-managed KMS keys and keys are never persistently stored in plaintext by Redwood components
Uploads support resume after network interruption with idempotent manifest and multipart reconciliation
Audit delivery is verifiable: per-blob manifest with SHA256 and delivery status visible in Console (delivered, pending, failed)
E2E test harness exists that can simulate 1GB backlog and show graceful backpressure, retry, and tombstoning behavior
Security review sign-off obtained and threat model added to the RFC
Migration path and rollback plan documented for customers moving from Redwood-managed storage to customer-managed storage
technical_notes: Architecture: introduce ForwarderCore + Adapter abstraction. ForwarderCore handles tenant queuing, policy enforcement, backpressure and retries. Adapter implementations handle sink-specific auth/transfer details.

Auth patterns: support (A) short-lived signed URLs (brokered by control plane), (B) pre-authorized credentials stored in sealed KMS vault (for dedicated/private), (C) direct CMEK handshake flow to enable server-side encryption with customer keys.

Transfer: use multipart uploads with per-part hashing + manifest file. Maintain a small on-disk transfer journal to resume in case of process restart. Journal entries rotated under tenant retention policy.

Backpressure: soft-queue with per-tenant concurrency limits derived from Dedicated capacity allocation. When DB-backed queue exceeds threshold, mark tenant delivery as degraded and surface in Console SLO dashboard.
Observability: emit delivery spans, per-tenant TTL metrics, retry counts, last-success timestamp; add a console view for queued bytes by tenant and sink.
Compatibility: Adapters should be pluggable for customer-provided binaries in airgap mode; document adapter contract and minimal deps.
Security: enforce mTLS to on-prem sinks where available, verify server cert chains against tenant-supplied CA bundle; fall back to signed-URL mode for environments that forbid inbound connectivity.
Performance: tune part size heuristics for high-latency links (e.g., 32MB for geo cross-region), expose config knobs per-deployment.
Legal/compliance: manifests must carry immutable metadata (tenant_id, export_window, retention_policy_ver, schema_version) to satisfy auditors.
Data lifecycle: implement tombstone/soft-delete marker for objects when customer retention triggers deletion; allow customer-initiated purge hooks via the control plane.
Testing: provide integration harness for Azure/GCS/S3 and a local SFTP appliance container for CI; add noise tests: packet loss, mid-upload reboot, time-skewed signed URLs.
Rollout: staged feature flag per-customer with canary on 3 low-volume tenants, observe delivery SLAs for 72h before enabling broadly.
decisions: Selected a pull-over-push hybrid: control plane brokers signed URLs for most sinks, but for air-gapped/on-prem appliances we support a pull-agent (customer-run) that fetches from a secure egress endpoint. This minimizes inbound firewall changes for customers.
Adopted multipart manifest + SHA256 verification to provide cryptographic proof-of-delivery rather than relying solely on service-level success codes.
CMEK handshake will use ephemeral wrapping keys exchanged via customer-provided KMS policy to avoid persistent key material storage in Redwood.
Adapter abstraction chosen to allow future addition of non-object sinks (Tape-archive connectors, SIEM endpoints) without changing core queuing logic.
We will not ship a default long-term retention store under this ticket; rather, we implement policy controls and connectors that enable customers to elect cold storage (their choice of backend).
comments: 2026-02-26 — Kickoff: scoped core requirements with PM and compliance. Decided to prioritize S3/SAS/SFTP adapters and leave Tape/Specialized appliances to later.
2026-03-03 — Spike complete: validated multipart resume for S3 via pre-signed multipart URLs. Observed 3x improvement in restart time vs naive re-upload for 512MB parts.
2026-03-06 — Security review: initial threat model posted; noted risk around signed-URL lifetimes and replay — added requirement for one-time-use nonces in manifest. Assigned follow-up to ENG-52011.
2026-03-09 — PR #5712 opened for ForwarderCore queue and Adapter interface. Need design feedback from Storage team on retry semantics (exponential vs. capped linear).
2026-03-11 — Design review: Platform lead requested per-tenant egress budget metric to avoid noisy-neighbor issues; added to scope as low-effort metric + alert.
2026-03-14 — Work in progress: adapter skeletons for S3 and SFTP merged to feature branch. Next: add CMEK handshake and end-to-end integration tests with local SFTP appliance container.
